newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close 1.98 pct up on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close 1.98 pct up on foreign buying.

text.p: Thai stocks closed 1.98 percent higher in moderate trade on Friday as foreigners bought large capitalised stocks after hearing the government was due to present its economic rehabilitation plan soon, brokers said.

"Foreigners bought finance, bank and communication issues upon learning that the government would unveil a comprehesive economic rehabilitation plan early next month," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
The composite SET index rose 12.58 points to 646.58 on 5.4 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 1.12 points to 48.80.

Government sources said shortly before the market closed that the major economic rehabilitation package that Thailand planed to unveil on August 5 would include measures to stabilise the baht and cure ills in the finance and property sectors.
The seven-point plan, believed to be set in a white paper, would be discussed and approved by the cabinet on August 5 and announced on the same day, they told Reuters.
"The economic plan has lifted market sentiment which was shrouded with worries over high domestic interest rates and a fall in the baht," said another broker.
All major sectors rose except the chemicals and plastics counter which dropped 0.50 percent.
The finance sector was first-ranked in terms of value, rising 5.68 percent, followed by the banking sector, which gained 2.28 percent. The communication sector advanced 4.04 percent.
Nava Finance topped the active list, rising 2.50 baht to 29.25. Bangkok Bank rose two to 171 and Advanced Info rallied 16 to 228.
